html:
New South Wales in 1815 was the British penal colony founded at Sydney in 1788. On paper it claimed the whole eastern half of Australia, west to the 135th meridian, which is why the map shows it so large; in fact settlers held only a small area around Sydney, Parramatta and the Hawkesbury River, with outposts in Van Diemen's Land and at Newcastle.

Most people were convicts or former convicts, sent by transportation since the First Fleet. The governor from 1810 to 1821, Lachlan Macquarie, set out to turn the jail into a town. He built roads and public buildings and gave freed convicts posts and respect, which angered many free settlers.

  • In 1813 Blaxland, Lawson and Wentworth found a way across the Blue Mountains, which had hemmed in the colony.
  • Convicts built a road over them, and Macquarie founded Bathurst beyond in 1815.

The move inland took the land of Aboriginal peoples such as the Wiradjuri. Near Sydney, fighting with the Dharug and their neighbours ended with the Appin massacre of 1816. In 1901 it became a state of Australia. Its later story is under New South Wales (UK).
